result:
The proposed answer of 1 is probably wrong, but I can't verify the reference value.

The argument has a plausible core. Near a critical layer, the neutral Rayleigh-type mode has streamfunction $\psi \sim \delta\ln|\delta|$, so $u' = \psi_y \sim \ln|\delta|$ and $\rho' \sim \ln|\delta|$. Since $\ln|\delta| \in H^s$ exactly for $s<1/2$ in one dimension, this gives $s_v = s_\rho = 1/2$. The gap is that the problem's critical exponents are defined through sharp constructions and non-existence results for a distorted Rayleigh operator. Generic logarithmic behaviour at a critical layer does not by itself establish that these are the sharp thresholds. I recall that results in this line of work state velocity thresholds of the form $3/2$ (with a $\pm\tau$ margin) rather than $1/2$, which would give a sum of 2. I have not verified this against the source paper, and the recollection is uncertain.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 2
